preconditions.description: Input consists of two integers n (3 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^5) and k (2 ≤ k ≤ n - 1), where n is the total number of nodes and k is the number of exit-nodes.

postconditions.expression: stdout.splitlines()[0].strip() == str(min_distance) and len(stdout.splitlines()) == n - 1 and all(len(line.split()) == 2 for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:])
postconditions.description: The first line of stdout is the minimum possible maximum distance (min_distance) between any two exit-nodes in the constructed network. The remaining n-1 lines describe the edges of the network, each as two integers representing connected nodes.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(node) <= n for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:] for node in line.split())
postconditions.description: All node IDs in the edges are within the valid range [1, n].
The network is a tree (connected and acyclic) with exactly n-1 edges.

postconditions.expression: exit_nodes := set(); exit_edges := sum(1 for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:] if (int(line.split()[0]) in exit_nodes) + (int(line.split()[1]) in exit_nodes) == 1); exit_nodes := set(); for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]: exit_nodes.update(line.split()); exit_nodes = exit_nodes if len(exit_nodes) == k else set(); len(exit_nodes) == k and exit_edges == k
postconditions.description: Exactly k nodes are exit-nodes (degree 1), and all other nodes have degree ≥ 2.

The maximum distance between any two exit-nodes in the constructed network equals the claimed minimum possible distance (min_distance). Here, exit_nodes_list is the list of exit-nodes, and adjacency_list is the adjacency representation of the network.
